system.name: Store
system.description: An online store that sells home goods to shoppers through a web shop and a mobile app, with internal tools for its fraud analysts and store managers.

corpus.included: Nothing real: the Store is an invented example, written by hand to teach the boundary model. No repository exists. The places and evidence name invented folders and files.
corpus.excluded: Shopper sign-in and accounts, saved cards and delivery addresses, which a real store would have. They are left out to keep the example small.

consumers.name: Shopper
consumers.description: A person who buys home goods from the Store, on the web or in the mobile app.

consumers.name: Fraud analyst
consumers.description: A Store employee who reviews the orders the fraud check flagged, and lets each one go ahead or cancels it.

consumers.name: Store manager
consumers.description: A Store employee who keeps the catalog right: the products, their prices and their stock.

providers.name: Store
providers.description: The online store as its shoppers and staff know it: the web shop, the mobile app and the staff tools.

parts.name: Web shop and mobile app clients
parts.why: They present the Store's capabilities to shoppers and keep nothing of their own, so they are parts of the web shop and mobile app interfaces.

parts.name: Mobile gateway
parts.why: It passes the mobile app's calls on to the components and trims the answers for small screens. It keeps nothing and decides nothing, so it is part of the mobile app interface.

parts.name: Dashboard, review console and store CLI
parts.why: Clients for staff, parts of their interfaces. The store CLI's database commands work on the system, so they are listed in excluded.

parts.name: Money library
parts.why: Rounds amounts and formats prices for every component. A library, not a component.

components.name: Storefront
components.description: Takes the shoppers' orders and keeps them, with each shopper's loyalty points. It prices, places, lists and cancels orders, decides how many points each order earns, and sends confirmed orders to the shipping partner.

parts.name: Order routes
parts.why: Receive the web shop's and mobile app's order requests and pass them on.

parts.name: Order database
parts.why: Where Storefront keeps orders and points. Only Storefront writes to it.

parts.name: Points rules
parts.why: How Storefront decides the points an order earns. A setting of Storefront, not a resource.

parts.name: Balance adjustments
parts.why: The records of points added and taken back, which add up to each balance. They are how Storefront keeps balances, not a resource.

components.name: Catalog
components.description: Keeps the products the Store sells, with their prices and stock, and alerts store managers when stock runs low.

parts.name: Catalog import
parts.why: Reads a catalog file and turns each row into a product change. It changes the same products as the rest of Catalog, so it is part of Catalog.

parts.name: Search index
parts.why: A copy of the products that makes browsing fast. Catalog rebuilds it, and it decides nothing.

components.name: Payments
components.description: Charges and refunds orders, and holds a risky payment until a fraud analyst decides.

parts.name: Outcome queue
parts.why: Carries the outcome of a held charge back to Storefront. It is how the charges API delivers its callback, not a component or a boundary.

components.name: Charge service
components.description: Runs each charge and refund: it asks Fraud check for a score, asks the card network for the money, and alone changes a charge's state.

parts.name: Card network adapter
parts.why: How Charge service reaches the card network API. Not a component.

components.name: Fraud check
components.description: Scores each payment, holds the risky ones for review, and keeps the analysts' reviews and their decisions.

parts.name: Scoring model
parts.why: How Fraud check decides a score. A set of rules or another model could replace it under the same contract, so it is an implementation choice, not a component.

parts.name: Scored charges
parts.why: Fraud check's own record of every charge it scored, kept apart from Charge service's charges. It is where Fraud check keeps its Charge resource.

outsideServices.name: Card network
outsideServices.description: The outside network that approves card payments and returns money to cards.

outsideServices.name: Shipping partner
outsideServices.description: An outside company that keeps the Store's goods in its warehouse, and packs and ships each order.

resources.name: Product
resources.description: Something the Store sells, with its price and its stock. A product can be on many orders.

resources.name: Order
resources.description: A shopper's purchase of one or more products. Each order belongs to one shopper.
properties: status: placed, on hold, confirmed, shipped, delivered or canceled

resources.name: Loyalty balance
resources.description: The points a shopper has earned from orders. Each shopper has one.
properties: points that expire next, and when

resources.name: Fraud review
resources.description: An analyst's case for one flagged order: why the fraud check held it, and what the analyst decided.
properties: status: open, let through or canceled

resources.name: Charge
resources.description: The money taken for one order, and any refunds of it. Each order has one charge.
properties: status: paid, declined, on hold or refunded

resources.name: Card authorization
resources.description: The card network's approval of one card payment, and the money returned against it.

resources.name: Shipment
resources.description: The parcel the shipping partner sends for one order.

interfaces.name: web shop
interfaces.description: The Store's website, where shoppers browse, order, and follow and cancel their orders.

interfaces.name: mobile app
interfaces.description: The Store's phone app. It offers what the web shop offers, and uses the phone's camera to show a product in the shopper's room.

interfaces.name: review console
interfaces.description: The internal website where fraud analysts work through flagged orders.

interfaces.name: dashboard
interfaces.description: The internal website where store managers edit products and get low-stock notices.

interfaces.name: store CLI
interfaces.description: The `store` command that store managers run to list products and import a catalog file.

interfaces.name: catalog API
interfaces.description: Catalog's contract for looking up products, and for reserving and releasing their stock.

interfaces.name: charges API
interfaces.description: Payments' contract for charging and refunding orders. It also brings back the outcome of a held charge.

interfaces.name: shipping API
interfaces.description: The shipping partner's contract for sending orders. It also brings back each parcel's delivery status.

interfaces.name: fraud scoring API
interfaces.description: Fraud check's contract for scoring a payment. It also brings back the analyst's decision on a held one.

interfaces.name: card network API
interfaces.description: The card network's contract for approving card payments and returning money to cards.

areas.name: Shop
areas.description: Find products, buy them, and follow or cancel what was bought.

capabilities.name: Browse products
capabilities.takes: a search or a category
capabilities.gives: the matching products, with their prices and whether they are in stock

capabilities.name: Place order
capabilities.takes: a cart, a delivery address and a card
capabilities.gives: the order, confirmed or on hold for review, with the points it earned; or a declined card to try again

capabilities.name: List past orders
capabilities.takes: the shopper's account
capabilities.gives: the shopper's orders, with their status, total and tracking number

capabilities.name: Cancel order
capabilities.takes: an order that has not shipped yet
capabilities.gives: the order canceled, its money refunded to the card, and its points taken back

areas.name: See product in your room
areas.description: See how a product would look, at its real size, in a room at home.

capabilities.name: See product in your room
capabilities.takes: a product, and the phone's camera pointed at a room
capabilities.gives: the product drawn at its real size in the camera's view of the room

areas.name: See loyalty balance
areas.description: See the points earned from past orders.

capabilities.name: See loyalty balance
capabilities.takes: the shopper's account
capabilities.gives: the points balance, and the points that expire next

evidence.shows: the checkout, where a shopper places an order and tries another card after a decline
past orders, with a cancel button on orders that have not shipped
the camera view that draws a product in a room, which the web shop does not have

areas.name: Review flagged orders
areas.description: Decide on each order the fraud check held, before it ships.

capabilities.name: List fraud reviews
capabilities.takes: open reviews, or a search by order or shopper
capabilities.gives: the flagged orders, each with its lines, its shopper, its score and the reasons for it

capabilities.name: Decide fraud review
capabilities.takes: a review, and a decision: let the order through or cancel it
capabilities.gives: the review closed with its decision; the order goes ahead, or is canceled without charging the shopper

evidence.shows: the list of open fraud reviews, and the buttons that let an order through or cancel it

areas.name: Keep the catalog right
areas.description: Keep the products, their prices and their stock right.

capabilities.name: List products
capabilities.takes: a search, or a filter such as low stock or hidden
capabilities.gives: the products, with their prices, their stock and whether shoppers can see them

capabilities.name: Edit product
capabilities.takes: a product and what to change: its name, description, price, stock or low-stock threshold, or whether shoppers see it
capabilities.gives: the product as shoppers will now see it

capabilities.name: Import catalog
capabilities.takes: a catalog file, with one row per product
capabilities.gives: the products added or changed, and the rows that could not be read

capabilities.name: Alert on low stock
capabilities.takes: the low-stock thresholds set on products
capabilities.gives: a notice in the dashboard whenever a product's stock falls below its threshold

evidence.shows: the product list and the product editor
the notices raised when a product's stock falls below its threshold
the import command, which reads a catalog file and reports the rows it could not read
the products command, which lists products

areas.name: Get products for orders
areas.description: Get the current prices of an order's products, and hold or release their stock.

capabilities.name: Look up products
capabilities.takes: product numbers
capabilities.gives: each product's name, price and stock

capabilities.name: Reserve stock
capabilities.takes: an order's lines
capabilities.gives: the stock held for the order, or the lines that are out of stock

capabilities.name: Release stock
capabilities.takes: the lines of a canceled order
capabilities.gives: that stock back on sale

evidence.shows: the catalog API's lookUpProducts, reserveStock and releaseStock operations

areas.name: Charge orders
areas.description: Take the money for an order, and give it back.

capabilities.name: Charge order
capabilities.takes: an order's total and the shopper's card
capabilities.gives: the charge, paid, declined or on hold; a held charge's outcome comes back on the charges API once an analyst decides

capabilities.name: Refund order
capabilities.takes: a charge, and the amount to give back
capabilities.gives: the charge, with that amount refunded to the card

evidence.shows: the charges API's chargeOrder and refundOrder operations, and the chargeSettled callback for held charges

areas.name: Ship order
areas.description: Get a confirmed order packed and sent to the shopper.

capabilities.name: Ship order
capabilities.takes: a confirmed order, with its delivery address
capabilities.gives: a shipment with its tracking number, then its delivery status as the parcel moves

evidence.shows: the calls to the shipping partner's API, and the handler for its delivery updates

areas.name: Take card payments
areas.description: Get card payments approved, and return money to cards.

capabilities.name: Authorize card payment
capabilities.takes: a card and an amount
capabilities.gives: an authorization or a decline

capabilities.name: Refund card payment
capabilities.takes: an authorization, and the amount to return
capabilities.gives: the amount returned to the card

evidence.shows: the authorize and refund calls to the card network API

areas.name: Score payment
areas.description: Learn whether a payment may go ahead.

capabilities.name: Score payment
capabilities.takes: a charge, with its order and card details
capabilities.gives: a score and a verdict: go ahead, decline or hold; for a held payment, the analyst's decision follows

evidence.shows: the fraud scoring API's scorePayment operation, and the reviewDecided callback

areas.name: Take card payments
areas.description: Get card payments approved, and return money to cards.

capabilities.name: Authorize card payment
capabilities.takes: a card and an amount
capabilities.gives: an authorization or a decline

capabilities.name: Refund card payment
capabilities.takes: an authorization, and the amount to return
capabilities.gives: the amount returned to the card

evidence.shows: the authorize and refund calls to the card network API

questions.question: Is the review console part of the Store, or a fraud tool of its own?
questions.answer: Part of the Store rather than its own provider. It ships with the Store, works on the Store's orders and fraud reviews, and keeps no data of its own, so analysts see it as the Store's back office. It would be its own provider if analysts used it as a separate product, with its own data.

questions.question: Do loyalty points belong to Storefront, or to a Loyalty component of their own?
questions.answer: To Storefront rather than a Loyalty component. Points change only when orders do, so the simplest model keeps them with the orders. A Loyalty component would fit a store whose points rules change apart from its orders, or that awards points for more than orders.

questions.question: Is seeing a product in your room a capability, or another view inside Browse products?
questions.answer: A capability rather than a view inside Browse products. Shoppers come to it with a goal of its own, deciding whether a product fits a room, and it takes something Browse products does not: the camera's view of the room.

questions.question: Does Storefront serve the fraud analyst?
questions.answer: Yes, beside Payments, rather than Payments alone. An analyst's decision lets an order through or cancels it, and only Storefront changes orders: it does so when the held charge's outcome comes back on the charges API.

cleanupCandidates.name: Old checkout
cleanupCandidates.why: apps/web-shop/src/legacy-checkout is the checkout the web shop used before the current one. A flag still turns it on, but no shopper reaches it.

excluded.name: Database commands of the store CLI
excluded.why: `store migrate` and `store seed` change the database schema and load test data. They work on the system, not with it.

excluded.name: Fraud model training
excluded.why: ml/fraud-model trains the model Fraud check scores with. It changes how the system decides, so it works on the system.

excluded.name: Deploy and infrastructure
excluded.why: infra/ and the CI workflows build and ship the Store.

excluded.name: Flagging risky payments
excluded.why: Fraud check flags payments on its own, as part of scoring them. No consumer asks for it: analysts review what it flagged.

excluded.name: Points expiry
excluded.why: Storefront expires points a year after they are earned, on its own. Shoppers see the points that expire next on their balance.

excluded.name: Search index rebuild and health checks
excluded.why: Machinery that keeps browsing fast and the services up. Nobody uses it for a purpose of their own.
